newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 14.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 32.52 points to 7,928.32 after news that U.S. producer prices fell for a seventh straight month in July.

* The Indonesian government will not hike telephone fees despite higher costs due to the depreciation of the rupiah against the U.S. dollar as the government would put the interests of customers as the top priority, Director General of Post and Telecommunications Djakaria Purawidjaja was quoted as saying by Neraca daily.
* Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, has said it will abolish the daily announcements of its intervention and conversion bands.

* On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index ended down 4.34 points, or 0.66 percent, at 658.60 points on the back of the central bank's decision to raise interest rates and the rupiah's plunge to a historic low.
* The Indonesian rupiah was quoted at 2,636.00/41.00 against the dollar at 0205 GMT compared with 2,648.00/58.00 at the opening.
* Telecommunications firm Telkom and Indosat on a Neraca newspaper report that the government did not plan to hike telephone fees despite depreciation of the rupiah against the dollar.
* Bakrie's telecommunications unit Ratelindo after the firm launched a new wireless data communications system.
* Retailer Ramayana, conglomerate Astra, bank BNI and automobile component firm Selamat Sempurna following announcements of first half results.
* Cigarette firms and Sampoerna on reports the government had decided to stop the conversion of clove trees into other crops as cigarette makers' demand for the spice was on the rise.
* Commodities related companies Mayora, Indofood, Prasidha and Budi Acid on the likelihood that an ongoing drought will be prolonged.
